Biggest leaks (estimated, overlapping, not additive)
  1. Repeated tool results: ~$4.50 (estimated), 60K tokens (estimated)
     Do this: duplicate_result_collapser = "on"
     Add this line under [optimizers] in config.toml. It applies from your next
     session.
  2. Noisy tool output: ~$3.00 (estimated), 90K tokens (estimated)
     Do this: trove optimize status
     noise_normalizer is on. See what it saved under Optimizers.
  3. Prompt cache misses: ~$1.35 (estimated), 27K tokens (estimated)
     Cache misses happen when the start of a request changes between turns.
     Avoid editing early context mid-session.

Optimizers
  volatile_prefix_mover: off
  noise_normalizer: on
    Saved ~$0.50 (estimated).
  output_trimmer: off
  duplicate_result_collapser: off
    Would have saved ~$3.60 (estimated, shadow mode).
    To turn on, add under [optimizers] in config.toml:
    duplicate_result_collapser = "on"
  cache_breakpoints: off
  Guardrail events: none.
  No regression detected locally. Trove checks retries, tool errors and
  re-fetches; it does not prove output quality.

Recommendations (suggestions only; Trove changes nothing on its own)
  1. Try hook_large_output in shadow mode (confidence: low)
     Tool results in this repo average 4.0 large outputs per session over 6
     sessions, and a go_test test setup was detected. The large-output hint
     suggests the trove_run tool for noisy commands; in shadow mode it only
     counts.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
  2. Try hook_quiet_commands in shadow mode (confidence: low)
     A go_test test setup was detected and tool results here average 4.0 large
     outputs per session. Quiet flags on test commands in shadow mode estimate
     the saving.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
  3. Try hook_read_limit in shadow mode (confidence: low)
     This repo is in size bucket L and sessions read about 30 files each. Line
     limits on big reads in shadow mode estimate what they would save.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
  4. Try hook_repeat_read in shadow mode (confidence: low)
     Sessions here re-read a file already read about 3.0 times each (over 6
     sessions). Repeat-read prevention in shadow mode counts how many reads it
     would have avoided.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
  5. Try output_trimmer in shadow mode (confidence: low)
     Over your last 6 sessions in this repo, tool results averaged 4.0 per
     session over 6,000 bytes. The output trimmer keeps failures and a summary
     and shortens the rest; in shadow mode it only estimates what it would
     remove.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
  6. Use the quick-fix settings profile (confidence: low)
     You said the task is quick-fix. Trove has a settings profile for it (`trove
     settings`). It has no benchmark behind it yet, so values without evidence
     are left out unless you allow them.
     A rule of thumb with no benchmark or measurement behind it yet (defaults
     seed-1; estimated). No savings figure.
